answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond in the jade ledger, and all its actions enter through one inlet so its timing and choices are logged. A crystal auditor recomputes correlation each epoch; identities over 80% alike form one group. The k-th identity in a group pays 70 plus 10(k-1) credits, so 1,000 correlated fakes cost 5,065,000 credits, superlinear and unmerged. A staggered-operator ring fails because the auditor also matches choices and counterparties, so staggered fakes still cluster. An honest agent pays 70 once and recovers its bond.
